faq.a: Outside the town, the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, under Electoral Area H Zoning Bylaw No. 3065, 2024 (adopted July 25, 2024). Inside the town, the Town of Princeton.

faq.q: Is Princeton acreage in the ALR?
faq.a: Some is and some is not. Check the parcel with the Agricultural Land Commission before you plan a second home, a subdivision or any non-farm use.

faq.q: What should I test on a rural Princeton property?
faq.a: The well (flow and water quality), the septic system, the floodplain status near the rivers, wildfire risk for insurance, and the legal access to the property.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

Most acreage around Princeton is outside the town, in Electoral Area H of the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, along the Similkameen and Tulameen valleys and the highways out of town. This search lists properties of one acre or more around Princeton.

items.t: Zoning:

Electoral Area H Zoning Bylaw No. 3065, 2024, adopted July 25, 2024, replaced Bylaw No. 2498, 2012. It was rewritten for the Province’s small-scale housing law and sets building types, density, setbacks, height and parcel coverage for each zone.
Community plan:
the Area H Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 2497, 2012.
Agricultural Land Reserve:
check whether the parcel is in the ALR before planning a second home, a subdivision or a non-farm use; the Agricultural Land Commission sets those rules, not the zoning.
Subdivision
of rural land goes through the Province’s approving officer as well as the zoning, so confirm the minimum parcel size for the zone before you count on splitting a lot.

blocks.text: Before you buy an acreage near Princeton

items.t: Well:
a flow test and a water quality test, and the well record if there is one.
Septic:
an inspection, and the filing record for the system.
Flood:
low land along either river can flood; the November 2021 flood hit both valleys. Check floodplain maps and get an insurance quote early.
Wildfire:
ask your insurer about the property’s wildfire rating and look at the FireSmart condition of the buildings and the trees around them.
Access:
confirm the road is public or that a registered easement covers the driveway, and who ploughs it in winter.
